Theorem
[Differential Harnack estimate for mean curvature flow] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0330, chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0331 1. ch15:15.42\group Related Harnack Estimates

Let a closed manifold evolve by a strictly convex mean curvature flow $\partial _tX=-H u $ in Euclidean space. Then \[ \partial _tH+ rac{H}{2t}-h^{-1}( abla H, abla H)\ge 0. \]
Proof

\sketch Denote the left side by $Z$. Direct differentiation of the mean-curvature and second-fundamental-form evolution equations, followed by completing the quadratic terms, gives

\[ (\partial _t-\Delta )Z =2g^{ij}(h^{-1})^{k\ell }J_{ik}J_{j\ell } +\left(|h|^2- rac2t ight)Z, \]

where

\[ J_{ik}= abla _i abla _kH+H(h^2)_{ik} -(h^{-1})^{pq} abla _pH abla _qh_{ik}+ rac1{2t}h_{ik}. \]

Strict convexity makes the first term nonnegative. The scalar maximum principle, beginning at small positive time where the $H/(2t)$ term dominates, yields $Z\ge 0$.

□
